title: CT-based AI risk support for cystic renal masses: multicenter validation, reader study, and a randomized implementation study
summary: In a randomized implementation phase involving 5,869 adults at one hospital, the post-hoc intention-to-treat proportion with benign pathology among all randomized patients was lower with AI-assisted reporting (0.95% vs 3.54%; risk difference −2.59 percentage points, 95% CI −3.38 to −1.85). Among treated lesions, benign pathology was 16.4% vs 40.3%, but the intended-use cystic renal mass subgroup difference was not statistically significant. Retrospective development followed by external validation at five hospitals (AUROC 0.913–0.999; one external set had only three malignant cases), a six-radiologist reader study (AUROC 0.825 unaided to 0.973 aided; mean reading time 9.7 to 5.5 minutes), and a randomized implementation study. Caveats: single-centre, developer-run implementation; treated-lesion endpoint conditions on post-randomization treatment; subgroup result not significant; no long-term cancer outcome or safety evidence.
ai_technology: KITE-CRM is a deep-learning pathway using corticomedullary-phase contrast-enhanced CT as its sole model input to estimate lesion-level malignancy risk and support radiologist reporting; clinicians retained treatment decisions.
